catalog_quote: Mada has no long or doubled vowels except in ideophones and exclamations. 2.1.3 Tones Mada has three level tones and a rising and falling tone. Tones are marked in the orthography and in this document as follows: high tone is unmarked /ˉ/ mid tone is shown by a macron /`/ for a low tone /ˆ/ for a falling tone /ˇ/ for a rising tone. The rising tone is uncommon compared with the other tones. Mada is highly tonal and many lexical and grammatical distinctions are made only by tone. The orthography therefore marks tone on all syllables. Mada distinguishes between tone-bearing and non-tone-bearing nasals, and several words have contrastive tone on a syllabic nasal in final position. Thus; kpm̀ ‘kapok tree’ Price (1989: 16) notes one example of downstep, with the third person singular pronoun kә ...

tone_statements.quote: In expressing ordinal class, from the foregoing, there is always a change in tone. For example, tàr represents the cardinal 3 and tǎr denotes 3rd as in the position of something.

tone_statements.summary: Grammatical tone stated for cardinal->ordinal derivation (low or mid -> rising in the examples: tàr/tǎr, tānnɛ̀n/tǎnnɛn); transcription uses four tone marks (unmarked H, macron M, grave L, caron R); no inventory statement, no stress statement.

tone_statements.citation: Samuel, Nuhu Baba. 2018. The Structure of Noun Phrase in Màda. Journal of the Linguistic Association of Nigeria (JOLAN), Supplement Volume III: 338-353. (Department of Languages and Linguistics, Nasarawa State University, Keffi.)
tone_statements.quote: The findings show that Màda attests three level tones with the high tone unmarked and two-tone glides - high-low/^/ and low-high /˅/ respectively. ... (1) Màda exhibits three contrastive level tones and they are very productive in initiating meaning contrast in the language, (2) the pitch pattern accommodates tone glide as shown in some examples above- gbǎ (cock) and gblǎ (weeding) ... Above all, mid-level tone, also known as intermediate pitch, completes the tone paradigm of Màda as a register tone language.
tone_statements.locator: Abstract p. 271; section 4.1 p. 280 (observations after minimal-pair test (3)); section 4.1 p. 283
tone_statements.summary: Three contrastive level tones (H, M, L) on the syllable, shown by minimal sets (zú/zù/zǔ, kúkú/kùkù/kūkū/kúkù/kùkú); rising/falling glides treated as two-tone glides; classed as a register-tone language. Tone marks plural, verbal nouns, questions. No acoustics; nothing on stress, downstep, floating.
